turns.text: Students at Lakeside College will be able to use a new evening shuttle between the library and the western residence halls from next week. The service is being introduced because the regular campus bus stops running at eight, while the library remains open until eleven. The college considered extending the regular route, but a smaller shuttle was found to be more practical for the number of passengers expected at night. It will depart every half hour from a stop beside the library entrance. Students will need to show a college card, but will not pay a fare. The shuttle will not call at the sports building, which already has a separate evening service. Transport staff will review passenger numbers at the end of the first six weeks. If demand is low on particular evenings, the timetable may change. The daytime campus bus schedule will remain as it is.

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: Visitors to the Marlow museum will soon see two kinds of label beside objects in its science gallery. One will give a brief explanation in everyday language. The other will provide technical details for visitors who want to explore the subject further. The museum began revising the labels after a visitor survey showed that many people stopped reading when they met an unfamiliar term in the first sentence. Staff initially tried removing all technical words, but teachers argued that students also needed opportunities to learn them. The two-label approach is intended to offer both an accessible starting point and a route to greater detail. The gallery will stay open while the labels are replaced, one display at a time. The museum has not purchased new objects for this project. It plans to ask visitors to compare the revised explanations with the earlier ones before changing labels in its other galleries.

turns.text: The Brookfield food festival is asking stallholders to use a shared collection point for reusable bowls this year. Visitors who choose a reusable bowl will pay a small deposit when they order food and receive the deposit back when they return the bowl. They can return it at the collection point even if they bought food from a stall at the other end of the festival. Last year's smaller trial required customers to find the original stall, and several said they kept the bowls because returning them was inconvenient. Festival staff will wash the returned bowls in a separate service area. Stallholders will still be responsible for serving food, but will not need to wash bowls themselves. Visitors may also bring their own clean containers. Organizers say the aim is to make returning shared bowls easier, rather than to ban every other type of container immediately. They will count how many bowls come back and compare the return rate with last year's trial before deciding on next year's arrangements.
